title: dbQuoteLiteral with MySQL 8.0
description:
DBI Version 1.2.3 changed the format returned by `dbQuoteLiteral()` for `POSIXct` values from `%Y%m%d%H%M%S` to `%Y-%m-%d %H-%M-%S%z`. This breaks support for MySQL 8.0, as the string is no longer recognized as a valid DATETIME string due to the added timezone info. 

It might be an issue with MySQL 8 or MySQL in general, but since I don't have a server of those other versions to check against, I can't tell for certain.

Since this seems to be an issue specific to MySQL 8.0, I'm filing it here, rather than with the DBI package itself. If this is wrong, please advise and I'll file it there, instead.

I also tried specifying the charset or the encoding in the dbConnect() stage, but that didn't seem to do anything. This is driving me crazy, please help.

title: Turn off column name mangling?
description:
`dbGetQuery()` and other `dbFetch`-based operations mangle the column names of the result if some of them are duplicated. This is done in `dbFetch()` by calling `RMariaDB:::set_tidy_names()` on the result.

How about making this mangling optional via a global option or an additional argument to `dbGetQuery`/`dbFetch`?

Problem with this mangling is that:
- it's inconsistent with the command line `mysql`/`mariadb` clients,
- it's not always desirable (I would even argue that it's almost never desirable),
- there's not reliable way to restore the real column names,
- it's inconsistent with **RSQLite** and **RMySQL**, two other members of the **DBI** family.

See https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/issues/308 for a previous discussion of column name mangling.

Thanks,
H.

title: Enabling secure (SSL/TLS) client connections, an example in documentation or a vignette would be nice
description:
The documentation could use an example of how to enable SSL/TLS connectivity without authentication (i.e., transport encryption). I would expect that this is fairly common scenario where the MariaDB server is configured to require secure transport via the [require-secure-transport](https://mariadb.com/kb/en/server-system-variables/#require_secure_transport) system variable.

In the legacy RMySQL library this is done with the via sslmode argument. It's not clear from the documentation how to do this with RMariaDB. The ssl.key, ssl.cert, ssl.ca and ssl.capath arguments all appear to deal with two-way TLS authentication. The client.flags argument appears to reference a CLIENT_SECURE_CONNECTION flag in the underlying C connector which appears to do what I want, however  there doesn't seem to be any CLIENT_SECURE_CONNECTION flag documented in the connector API's documentation on RMariaDB's [website](https://mariadb.com/kb/en/mysql_real_connect/).

I'm able to successfully connect to my particular database using RMySQL:

```r
library("RMySQL")

# connect to MySQL database
mysql_dbconn <- dbConnect(
    drv = RMySQL::MySQL(),
    dbname = "internal_equities",
    user = "MYSUSERNAME",
    password = "MYPASSWORD",
    sslmode = "require")
```

I'm sure I've missed something obvious so if someone has a working configuration please share it. 

I'd also love to see the documentation include an example and the client.flags documentation updated if it is indeed the case that the CLIENT_SECURE_CONNECTION flag is no longer used by the connector.

Thanks

description:

Here is my code:

```
# loading packages

library(RMariaDB)

# create twitter api token

tweets$Topic <- "beautiful"

title: dbQuoteIdentifier() does not allow columns in Id() object.
description:
Like [RPostgres](https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/issues/263), RMariaDB does not allow to quote column identifiers (the last example of [`glue::glue_sql()`](https://glue.tidyverse.org/reference/glue_sql.html) relies on this feature).

``` r
library(RMariaDB)
con <- mariadbDefault()

column_id <- Id(table = "mytable", column = "mycolumn")
dbQuoteIdentifier(con, column_id)
#> Error in dbQuoteIdentifier(con, column_id): all(names(x@name) %in% c("schema", "table")) is not TRUE
```

In addition it is not possible to quote a valid schema identifier, again similar to [RPostgres](https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/pull/372#issuecomment-1002105174)

``` r
(schema_id <- dbQuoteIdentifier(con, Id(schema = "myschema")))
#> <SQL> `myschema`.
```

Note the dot behind the quoted schema name.

``` r
statement <- paste0("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS ", schema_id)
dbExecute(con, statement)
#> Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near '.' at line 1 [1064]

dbDisconnect(con)
```

title: Documentation of differences between RMariaDB and RMySQL regarding data types?
description: Hi, my team is currently trying to migrate from RMySQL to RMariaDB. For the biggest part it's working well, but we do have some trouble regarding the differences both packages have regarding the translation of MySQL data types to R data types. For example, MySQL `DATETIME` is loaded by RMySQL as `character` and by RMariaDB as `POSIXct`. These changes are totally reasonable, but currently our only way of noticing them is when errors are thrown on downstream function calls. I tried to find some documentation that covers these differences but couldn't find anything. Does something like this exists or would it be possible to create it?

title: LOAD DATA executions not returning affected rows value
description:
Hi there,

I believe there is a bug in the returned 'affected rows' value that results after executing a LOAD DATA command. I am running on windows 10, and connecting to a cloud based MySQL database 5.7

Hopefully the following reprex is satisfactory. It uses a temporary table for reproducability, but the result is the same with permanent tables.

```r
db_temp_table_name <- "temp_table123"
temp_file_name <- tempfile("temp123.csv")
temp_file_name <- stringr::str_replace_all(temp_file_name, "\\\\", "/")

local_temp_table <- data.frame(id = 1:10)
write.csv(local_temp_table, temp_file_name)

sql_create_table <-
  paste(
    "CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ", db_temp_table_name, "
    (id INT)
   ENGINE=InnoDB"
  )

sql_load_data <-
  paste0(
    "LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '", temp_file_name, "'
    INTO TABLE ", db_temp_table_name, "
    FIELDS TERMINATED BY ',' ENCLOSED BY '\"' ESCAPED BY '\\\\'
    LINES TERMINATED BY '\\r\\n'
    IGNORE 1 LINES
    (`id`)"
  )

mariadb_con <-
  RMariaDB::dbConnect(
    RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
    host = ...,
    user = ...,
    password = ...,
    port = ...,
    dbname = ...,
    bigint = "numeric"
  )

RMariaDB::dbExecute(conn = mariadb_con, statement = sql_create_table)
RMariaDB::dbGetQuery(conn = mariadb_con, "select * from temp_table123")
affected_records <- RMariaDB::dbExecute(conn = mariadb_con, statement = sql_load_data)
affected_records ## has value 0, but should have value 10
RMariaDB::dbGetQuery(conn = mariadb_con, "select * from temp_table123") ## confirm that the insert did infact occur.
RMariaDB::dbDisconnect(mariadb_con)
```
For comparison reasons, it is worth noting that when using RMySQL the correct 'affected rows' value is returned, so the value is presumably being returned by the database. I am working on a project where confirmation that the correct number of inserts has occurred is necessary, and so this issue is preventing me from upgrading from RMySQL to RMariaDB.

Many thanks in advance. Appreciate the work you do.

title: TSLv1.3 bug
description:
There appears to be something bugged with TLSv1.3. My R code doesn't allow me to connect by using TLS certificates. I was able to connect from a Debian WSL2 VM on my Windows 11 machine without the SSL parameters to my MariaDB server (which is on my home server) via an unencrypted connection. 

I was also able to connect via SSL to the MariaDB server from the Debian WSL2 VM using the mysql command-line, so I'm positive I can connect to this database using SSL and using these exact certificates from my Windows 11/Debian VM machine. 

I have tried to execute the code below in both RStudio in Windows 11 Pro and in R-base on the Debian WSL2 VM, and get the same error from both, which suggests to me that its OS agnostic (baring any funny business with the way WSL2 works). 

Windows 11 is up-to-date and has TSLv1.3 enabled. The Debian VM is version 11. The MariaDB server is running on Ubuntu server 22.04.1 LTS. 

The error is:

Error: Failed to connect: SSL connection error: no cipher match. Error 0x80090331(SEC_E_ALGORITHM_MISMATCH)

```r
library(DBI)
library(pool)
library(RMariaDB)

pool <- dbPool(
  drv = RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
  dbname = "test",
  user = "user",
  host = "xx.xx.xx.xx",
  port = "3306",
  password = "xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  client.flag = CLIENT_SSL,
  ssl.key = "client-key.pem",
  ssl.cert = "client-cert.pem",
  ssl.ca = "ca-cert.pem",
  ssl.cipher = "TLSv1.3"
)
```
I have also tried removing client.flag, ssl.ca and ssl.cipher and they result in the same error. If I remove ssl.key or ssl.cert then I get a different error (that it cannot find a relevant PEM file). I should note that I haven't yet tried using a TSLv1.2 cipher to generate the certificates to see if that would work. I thought perhaps I should note it here to see if there was already a known issue.

title: Strange behaviour in data.table::foverlaps going from RMariaDB version 1.0.11 to version 1.1.0
description:
With RMariaDB versions >= 1.1.0 there is a strange interaction with `data.table::foverlaps` that does not happen in previous RMariaDB versions. In that case `data.table::foverlaps` errors if passed an empty `data.table::data.table` with date columns, with the error:
```r
Error in setkeyv(x, cols, verbose = verbose, physical = physical) :                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  Column 'pos' is type 'list' which is not supported as a key column type, currently.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Calls: <Anonymous> -> setkey -> setkeyv                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
In addition: Warning message:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
In structure(c(unlist(lapply(list(...), .recursive_date_unclass))),  :                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Calling 'structure(NULL, *)' is deprecated, as NULL cannot have attributes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Consider 'structure(list(), *)' instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
Execution halted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
```
This happens independently of the `data.table` package version, and only for RMariaDB versions >= 1.1.0, and only if an RMariaDB connection object has been created, even if the connection is never used and it is closed and removed before `data.table::foverlaps` is called.

---


Minimal working example (requires a database server to connect to but never actually uses the connection)
```r
con <- RMariaDB::dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), user="username", password="password"
        host="127.0.0.1", port=3306,
        dbname="dbname", default.file="/etc/mysql/my.cnf")
RMariaDB::dbDisconnect(con)
rm(con)

tab1 <- data.table::data.table(start=as.Date(integer(0), origin="1970-01-01"),
                               end=as.Date(integer(0), origin="1970-01-01"))
tab2 <- data.table::data.table(start=as.Date(integer(0), origin="1970-01-01"),
                               end=as.Date(integer(0), origin="1970-01-01"))

data.table::setkeyv( tab1, c("start", "end"))
data.table::setkeyv( tab2, c("start", "end"))
ret <- data.table::foverlaps(tab1, tab2)
```

Tested and found to succeed, with `data.table::foverlaps` returning an empty `data.table::data.table`, with RMariaDB versions up to 1.0.11, but from 1.1.0 the error described above is raised. Tested with multiple `data.table` versions: 1.10.0, 1.11.0, 1.12.0, 1.13.0, 1.14.0, 1.14.2 (most recent version as of submission) and success/failure independent of `data.table` version used:
`RMariaDB` version (top row) vs `data.table` version (left column)
|        | 1.0.10  | 1.0.11  | 1.1.0   | 1.2.0   | 1.2.1
|--------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| **1.10.0** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |
| **1.11.0** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |
| **1.12.0** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |
| **1.13.0** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |
| **1.14.0** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |
| **1.14.2** | Success | Success | Failure | Failure | Failure |

Tested on both Linux (Ubuntu 18.04 with R3.6.0 and R4.1.3) and on Windows 10 with a clean install of RStudio 2022.02.1+461  with R4.1.3

I'm not sure whether the actual bug is in `data.table` or `RMariaDB` and my internal R knowledge is not enough to pick it apart, but the bug does seem to have come about through a change in the `RMariaDB` package rather than the `data.table` package.

title: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE vs INSERT INTO
description: **Issue by [szilard](https://github.com/szilard)** _Saturday May 30, 2015 at 03:22 GMT_ _Originally opened as https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/issues/71_ ---- For dbWriteTable: - Latest CRAN version (0.10.3) uses LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/blob/april/R/table.R#L139 - Latest dev uses INSERT INTO https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/blob/master/R/table.R#L105 Most analytical/columnar/MPP databases (e.g. MySQL-based Infobright) strongly prefer "bulk loads", but my guess is that standard MySQL is faster with LOAD than with INSERT as well http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.0/en/insert-speed.html Also, the latest dev uses one INSERT per row rather then "bulk insert" (not to be confused with "bulk load") http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7977172/mysql-multiple-insert-performance Looping 1 row at a time is probably the slowest solution. Any comments @jeroenooms @hadley on why LOAD was changed to INSERT? PS: The way I found this is that the latest CRAN 0.10.3 does not work with Infobright (call it a "bug") as Infobright has different FIELDS TERMINATED BY defaults. Adding `FIELDS TERMINATED BY '\t'` here https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/blob/april/R/table.R#L141 would fix the issue on 0.10.3, but that's moot in dev (as LOAD was changed to INSERT).

title: Slow writing data to MySQL database hosted on Google Cloud
description:
I recently created a database using Google Cloud MySQL (2nd generation) and have been running into some performance issues trying to write data to the database via RMariaDB.  Observe the following...

```
# Connect to database using MariaDB driver (slow)
mycon <- DBI::dbConnect(
  drv = RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
  dbname = "mydb", 
  host = "11.111.111.111", 
  user = "foo",
  password = ""
)

# Write table 'iris'
system.time(RMariaDB::dbWriteTable(conn = mycon, name = "iris", value = iris, row.names = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE))
# 9.515 seconds

RMariaDB::dbDisconnect(mycon)

# Connect to database using MySQL driver (fast)
mycon <- DBI::dbConnect(
  drv = DBI::dbDriver("MySQL"),
  dbname = "mydb", 
  host = "11.111.111.111", 
  user = "foo",
  password = ""
)

# Write table 'iris'
system.time(RMariaDB::dbWriteTable(conn = mycon, name = "iris", value = iris, row.names = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE))
# 0.441 seconds

# Attempt 1 to append data to table
system.time(RMariaDB::dbAppendTable(conn = mycon, name = "iris", value = iris))
# Error in .local(conn, statement, ...) : 
#   unused argument (param = unname(as.list(value)))
# Timing stopped at: 0.005 0 0.005

# Attemp 2 to append data to table, using RMySQL
system.time(RMySQL::dbWriteTable(conn = mycon, name = "iris", value = iris, row.names = FALSE, overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE))
# 0.206 seconds

```

My questions are

1. *Should* it be possible to write data to a MySQL database on Google Cloud in a reasonable amount of time?  (Perhaps I am trying to do something that was not intended to be done.)
2. As shown by the error above, I cannot append data to a table using RMariaDB with a MySQL driver.  Is this a bug? 

For now I am stuck using RMySQL :/

Thanks, I **really** appreciate all the hard work done on this package!

title: dbWriteTable() much slower than RMySQL, especially slow on Mac
description:
RMySQL is orders of magnitude faster than RMariaDB, especially for writes. Tested on both OSX and Amazon Linux. Reading/writing from an AWS RDS database, MySQL v5.6.39. Also Amazon Linux is much faster than Mac, although I guess that could be a product of network speed. That is also a concern because we do some development on Macs. The reason I don't just switch to RMySQL is that RMariaDB handles unicode characters better than RMySQL, which is another important consideration.

### Script
There is a `DBI::dbWriteTable()` and `DBI::dbConnect()` in addition to `RMariaDB::dbWriteTable()` and `RMariaDB::dbConnect()`. To avoid any namespacing confusion, I ran everything with every combination of DBI, RMySQL, and RMariaDB.

Before running I uninstalled and reinstalled R packages.

I also installed `mariadb-devel` and `mysql-devel` on Linux and `mariadb-connector-c` and `mysql-connector-c` on Mac.

# detach("package:DBI", unload=T)
# remove.packages(c("DBI", "RMySQL", "RMariaDB"))
# install.packages(c("DBI", "RMySQL", "RMariaDB"))

# Amazon AMI

# sudo yum install mysql-devel

title: Perf issue with dbWriteTable : RMariaDB much slower than RMySQL (from 2 to 40 times), and it's worse with a remote db
description:
I experiment writing a table (a tibble: 34,951 x 52) into a MySQL database (5.6):

MySQL database on localhost (same computer):
- RMySQL    = 3.4s
- RMariaDB  = 8s

remote MySQL database: 
- RMySQL   = 11s
- RMariaDB : R still running after 5mn, i have to kill it

remote MySQL database with a reduced table (586 x 52): 
- RMySQL    = 0.4s
- RMariaDB  = 16s


```r
library(tidyverse) 
library(readxl) 
library(RMySQL) 
library(RMariaDB) 
library(curl) 

urlhebtour <- "https://insee.fr/fr/statistiques/fichier/2021703/base-cc-tourisme-2020.zip"
xlsfile    <- unzip( curl_download( urlhebtour, "temp.zip" ) )  

dt <- read_excel( xlsfile, sheet = "COM", skip = 5 ) %>% select(-LIBGEO) 

# RMySQL test on localhost
db_cred = list( drv = MySQL(), host="localhost", dbname="donstat", user="xxx", password="xxx" )
mycon <- exec( "dbConnect", !!!db_cred ) 

system.time( dbWriteTable( mycon, value = dt, name = "tourism2020", 
                                    overwrite = TRUE, row.names = FALSE ) )
# RMySQL 3.4s

tbl(mycon, "tourism2020") %>% collect()
# A tibble: 34,951 x 52

dbDisconnect(mycon)  

# RMariaDB test on localhost
db_cred <- list( drv = MariaDB(), host="localhost", dbname="donstat", user="xxx", password="xxx" )
mycon <- exec( "dbConnect", !!!db_cred ) 

system.time( dbWriteTable( mycon, value = dt, name = "tourism2020", 
                                       overwrite = TRUE, row.names = FALSE ) )
# RMariaDB 8s

tbl(mycon, "tourism2020") %>% collect()
# A tibble: 34,951 x 52
```

With a remote database and RMariaDB, it doesn't end

So let's try with a reduced tibble (=> 586 rows)
```r
system.time( dbWriteTable( mycon, value = dt %>% filter(DEP == "31"), name = "tourism2020", overwrite = TRUE, row.names = FALSE ) )

# RMySQL   = 0.4s
# RMariaDB = 16s
```

title: `~` not resolved correctly in `default.file` argument
description:
Hi,

on Windows 10 with R 4.0.2, after updating from RMariaDB 1.0.8 to 1.0.11, the following fails:

```r
library(RMariaDB)
dbConnect(MariaDB(), groups = "MYSQL", default.file = "~/.my.cnf")
```

The error message is `Failed to connect: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'localhost' (10061)`.

However, replacing the `~` as in 

```r
dbConnect(MariaDB(), groups = "MYSQL", default.file = file.path(Sys.getenv("R_USER"), ".my.cnf"))
```

works just fine. Any ideas why this could happen? The issue was not present before the package update. Edit: It also seems to work with version 1.0.10.

Many thanks in advance!

title: Transactions are not working as expected when used with INSERT-statements
description:
I have an MySQL server (v8.0.25) on my local Windows10 machine which I use to build up a database with a lot of tables and need to insert complicated data structures over connected tables. Therefore, I need to use transactions so that I can begin a transaction, then insert data in different tables, check if an error occures and to rollback all the inserts in this case. Otherwise some tables have orphaned entries which is a big problem...

But: I tested this with the RMySQL-package (which has no prepared statements, I think), with the odbc-package (which has strange issues regarding UTF-8 encoded inserts when using prepared statements) and with the RMariaDB-package (which works great regarding prepared statements and encoding, but need the old password hashing...as you already know). I am using the up-to-date mariadb connector for W10 64bit.

With none of these, transactions work as expected. They are ONLY working with the `RSQLite::SQLite()` in memory database as also used in the documentation of the DBI-package. Here is a reprex:

```r
library(DBI)
library(RMariaDB)

con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                 host     = "localhost",
                 port     = 3306,
                 username = keyring::key_list("mysql-localhost")[1,2],
                 password = keyring::key_get("mysql-localhost", "dataadmin")
)

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS `testdb`;")
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, paste0("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS `testdb` ",
                              "DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;"))
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "USE `testdb`;")
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS `testdb`.`Testtable` ;")
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, paste0("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `testdb`.`Testtable` ",
                              "(`idTesttable` INT NOT NULL, `comment` ",
                              "VARCHAR(255) NULL, PRIMARY KEY (`idTesttable`)) ",
                              "ENGINE = MyISAM ;"))
dbClearResult(rs)

data_in <- dbSendQuery(con,
                       paste0("INSERT INTO `testdb`.`Testtable` ",
                              "(`idTesttable`, `comment`) ",
                              "VALUES (1, 'Hallo');"))
dbClearResult(data_in)
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM testdb.Testtable")

# This gives:
#   idTesttable comment
# 1           1   Hallo

dbWithTransaction(
    con,
    {
        dbExecute(con,
                  paste0("INSERT INTO `testdb`.`Testtable` ",
                         "(`idTesttable`, `comment`) ",
                         "VALUES (2, 'Tschau');"))
        dbBreak()
    }
)
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM testdb.Testtable")

# This gives (but should give the same as before...):
#   idTesttable comment
# 1           1   Hallo
# 2           2  Tschau

dbBegin(con)

data_in <- dbSendQuery(con,
                       paste0("INSERT INTO `testdb`.`Testtable` ",
                              "(`idTesttable`, `comment`) ",
                              "VALUES (3, 'Ciao');"))
dbClearResult(data_in)
dbRollback(con)

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM testdb.Testtable")

# This gives (but should give the same as the first query...):
#   idTesttable comment
# 1           1   Hallo
# 2           2  Tschau
# 3           3    Ciao

```



I did try this with a locally installed mariadb-server, exactly the same behaviour. I did try different variants of this without calling `dbClearResults()` but only the additional warning, no different behaviour. I did try this with `dbSendStatement`, with `dbGetQuery` (additional warning) but without a different outcome. 

Please help!

P.S.: The R-Sig-DB mailing list server seems to be offline at the moment...

P.P.S.: Thanks a lot for your great work with this package, it works like a charm with everything else, only this issue causes me a headache!


------

Additional example which IS working:

```r
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                 host     = "localhost",
                 port     = 3306,
                 username = keyring::key_list("mysql-localhost")[1,2],
                 password = keyring::key_get("mysql-localhost", "dataadmin")
)

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS `testdb`;")
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, paste0("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS `testdb` ",
                              "DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;"))
dbClearResult(rs)
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "USE `testdb`;")
dbClearResult(rs)


df <- data.frame(id = 1:5)

dbWriteTable(con, "df", df)
dbBegin(con)
dbExecute(con, "UPDATE df SET id = id * 10")
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT id FROM df")
dbRollback(con)

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT id FROM df")
```

WHY? Only difference here is that the table is written into the DB with `dbWriteTable` at the beginning....

Hey there,
long awaited and now available, I was very happy about the possibility to insert data into MySQL databases via local file. However, I may have found a small issue when creating the TSV file.
{readr} seems to escape already escaped quotes, which leads to unwanted results. My suggestion would be to use `readr::write_delim(..., escape = "none")`, unless the default escaping of readr was chosen on purpose.

Cheers, 
Janis

```r
escape_testing <- function(escape = "double"){

title: NULL values in BIT(1) columns are returned as TRUE
description:
It seems that with version 1.1.0 `BIT(1)` columns that have `NULL` values return `TRUE` instead of `NA`. This might be a bug introduced in #192.

```r
library(RMariaDB)
con <- dbConnect(MariaDB(), dbname = "test")
dbWriteTable(con, "test", data.frame(a = c(NA_integer_, 0:1)), field.types = c(a = "BIT(1)"), overwrite = TRUE)
dbReadTable(con, "test")$a
#> [1] TRUE FALSE TRUE
```

The `dbWriteTable` call creates a table with the below CREATE statement. The table on the server does contain the values `NULL`, `0` and `1` on my MySQL instance (version 8).
```sql
CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `a` BIT(1) NULL DEFAULT NULL
)
```

The problem might be here, where `NA_INTEGER` is mapped to `1` it seems.
https://github.com/r-dbi/RMariaDB/blob/524135500b37790b33b895416d14613ee9874321/src/MariaRow.cpp#L216-L218

Happy to contribute a fix and thanks for all your work!

title: Consider respecting time zone of server
description:
Instead of setting the time zone, we could query it via

```sql
SELECT TIMEDIFF(NOW(), UTC_TIMESTAMP)
```

(from https://stackoverflow.com/a/3984412/946850) and add a `"tzone"` attribute to the times returned.

https://github.com/r-dbi/RMariaDB/issues/93#issuecomment-450565902

## Time zones are a mess

From https://github.com/r-dbi/RMariaDB/issues/80#issuecomment-353309883: RMariaDB doesn't set the `"tzone"` attribute for the date-times values it returns. This means that R will display times in your local time zone by default. Date values don't seem to have such an attribute:

``` r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB())
zero_time <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT from_unixtime(0)")[[1]]
zero_time
#> [1] "1970-01-01 01:00:00 CET"
lubridate::with_tz(zero_time, "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
```

Created on 2017-12-21 by the [reprex package](http://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.1.1.9000).

## Do settings affect the values we get from the driver? What time zone is the data stored in?

How does the `TIME_ZONE` variable we set affect the times returned?

MySQL doesn't store time zone information in a column/value. Is it always safe to assume that it's UTC or the server's time zone? Need to document the problem and possible solutions. Note that `TIMESTAMP` and `DATETIME` columns have different semantics.

``` r
library(DBI)

con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), dbname = "test")
dbWriteTable(
  con, "test",
  data.frame(timestamp = Sys.time(), datetime = Sys.time()),
  field.types = c("timestamp" = "TIMESTAMP", "datetime" = "DATETIME"),
  temporary = TRUE
)
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT NOW()")
#>                 NOW()
#> 1 2018-12-30 16:40:53
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM test")
#>             timestamp            datetime
#> 1 2018-12-30 16:40:53 2018-12-30 16:40:53

dbExecute(con, "SET time_zone = '-05:00'")
#> [1] 0
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT NOW()")
#>                 NOW()
#> 1 2018-12-30 11:40:53
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM test")
#>             timestamp            datetime
#> 1 2018-12-30 11:40:53 2018-12-30 16:40:53
```

<sup>Created on 2018-12-30 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1.9000)</sup>

## Why are DBItest tests not detecting the problems that the users see?

Should the tests require an explicit `"tzone"` attribute for datetime values?

## More info

- https://stackoverflow.com/a/19075291/946850
- https://javorszky.co.uk/2016/06/06/today-i-learned-about-mysql-and-timezones/
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/datetime.html

## Better documentation

Maybe a separate blog post?

title: Authentication fails because caching_sha2_password.dll doesn't exist
description:
When running this:

```r
test_db <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                       user='username',
                       password='password',
                       dbname='my_database',
                       host='localhost')
```
It fails with this error:
```
Error: Failed to connect: Plugin caching_sha2_password could not be loaded: The specified module could not be found.
```

It is apparently looking for **caching_sha2_password.dll** in all directories in my path:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/411495/97804863-1d390100-1c18-11eb-8af9-2d70504db020.png)

This won't work because the DLL does not exist. This is confirmed by a post of Georgi "Joro" Kodinov, MySQL SrvGen team lead, at https://forums.mysql.com/read.php?10,664655,664726. I have MySQL Connector C++ 8.0 installed, and I can confirm that this DLL is not included. (Yes, it's true that the path doesn't touch those the MySQL Connector's directories, but that's not relevant, since the file doesn't exist.)

Others have reported this error. Here's an example, which includes a workaround that appears to downgrade security: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54099722/how-to-connect-r-to-mysql-failed-to-connect-to-database-error-plugin-caching

I am running R 4.0.3 on Windows 10 2H20 with all R packages up to date.

While this seems to relate to #134, I am not sure it's the same. If it overlaps, then this issue provides some specific guidance to that other issue, at least for Windows users.

title: CLIENT_COMPRESS problem?
description:
I had everything working until I had the great idea to turn on the client compress flag as such:
MY_POOL=pool::dbPool(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                               client.flag=CLIENT_COMPRESS)

My database is very big, it does heavy computation. Everything was working until I had that idea. After that, on every collect() I got:
 big_coomputation()%>%collect(n=Inf)
Error: Lost connection to MySQL server during query [2013] 

After that mysql server gone away and etc... I had nothing interesting in my my.cnf except the packet size set to 1gb. Turned off CLIENT_COMPRESS and its all happy now.

Sorry to not be of more help here, or if this is obvious to someone. Just thought id pass on this problem here to see if it rings a bell.

        command: mysqld --character-set-server=utf8mb4 --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
        volumes:
            - ./mysql-dockerDB/var/lib/mysql:/var/lib/mysql
            - ./dockermnt:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
        container_name: mysqlDB
        restart: always
        ports:
            - '6603:3306'
        environment:
            MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
```

I expose the port 6603 to the localhost which allows me to access mysql in the container by i.e.:  
`mysql --host=localhost --port=6603 --user=root --password=secret --protocol=tcp`

### Problem
When I try to connect my local R Studio (not in docker) to mysqlDB via the open port with
```
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                  dbname = "dbname",
                  username = "root",
                  password = "secret",
                  port = 6603)
```
I get the error: `Error: Failed to connect: Can't connect to local MySQL server through socket '/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock' (2)
`. The same error happens when I specify `host = "localhost"` explicitly.
Which is unexpected, as I don't want to connect to the socket file rather using the TCP network protocol. 
Unfortunately the argument `protocol = "TCP"` is not supported.

### Workaround
I could solve the issue with specifying the protocol in the configuration file:

.my.cnf
```
[destination]
  port=6603
  proto=TCP
```
and then in R specifying the path to the configuration file and groups argument.
```
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                  dbname = "dbname",
                  username = "root",
                  password = "secret",
                  groups="destination",
                  default.file = "<path-to-configuration-file>/.my.cnf")
```
### Proposed Solution
In regard of the raising popularity of container stacks, it would be very valuable to have an argument in the method `dbConnect()` to directly specify the protocol type. Then, the workaround with the config file would be obsolete.
I imagine sth like this
```
con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                  dbname = "dbname",
                  username = "root",
                  password = "secret",
                  port = 6603,
                  protocol = "tcp")
```

title: Milliseconds from POSIXct timestamps does not appear in datetime(6) column in database
description:
I am trying to write a dataset with a column of timestamps to a database, using `dbWriteTable`. The timestamps are in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.ffff` for example `2020-01-15 09:13:35:3357`. I convert these to POSIXct so R can parse them.

```
dataframe$DateTime <- as.POSIXct(mydata$DateTime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS")
```

R will not print the milliseconds by default, but they can be seen if you run:
```
format(dataframe$DateTime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS4")
```

Then I try to send it to the database using a `datetime(6)` which should allow us to send timestamps with milliseconds:
```
dbWriteTable(mydb, "my_table", dataframe, append = TRUE, field.types = c(DateTime="datetime(6)"), row.names=FALSE)"
```

But when I send this to the database, the timestamp becomes `2020-01-15 09:13:35.000000` instead of `2020-01-15 09:13:35.335700`.

My suspicion was that some conversion is going on, which does not take milliseconds into account. So I tried keeping `mydata$DateTime` which is just a string - this, the `dbWriteTable` sends to the database just fine and the milliseconds remain.

Sorry, I am out of time right now but i can put a reprex later (otherwise hopefully this should be possible to reproduce using the code snippets I put above).

title: copy_to guesses column types better with RMySQL than RMariaDB
description:
With RMySQL, a "copy_to" exports a table by following the types and lengths of its columns quite precisely, for instance adjusting the type and computing the proper length for VARCHAR cols. It is really handy! 

With RMariaDB, the character columns are converted approximately (they are actually converted to blobs).

Could RMariaDB catch up with RMySQL in this respect?

Because it is quite painful to have to explicitly specify field.types (dbWriteTable) for all columns. Of course i could go on with RMySQL, but it is apparently no longer supported.

```r
library(tidyverse) 
library(RMySQL) 
library(RMariaDB) 

dt <- tribble(
  ~lib, ~id, ~x,
  "Bage-le-Chatel",     "01", 3,
  "Asnieres-sur-Saone", "02", 1,
  "Asnieres",           "03", 1,
)

# RMySQL
db_cred = list( drv = MySQL(), host="xxx", dbname="xxx", user="xxx", password="xxx" )
mycon <- exec( "dbConnect", !!!db_cred ) 

copy_to( mycon, dt, name = 'test', overwrite = T, temporary = FALSE ) 

dbExecute( mycon, "ALTER TABLE test ADD PRIMARY KEY(id)" )
rs <- dbSendQuery( mycon, "SHOW COLUMNS FROM test" )
dbFetch(rs)

##  Field        Type Null Key Default Extra
##1   lib varchar(18)  YES        <NA>      
##2    id  varchar(2)   NO PRI              
##3     x      double  YES        <NA> 

# RMariaDB
db_cred = list( drv = MariaDB(), host="xxx", dbname="xxx", user="xxx", password="xxx" )
mycon <- exec( "dbConnect", !!!db_cred ) 

copy_to( mycon, dt, name = 'test', overwrite = T, temporary = FALSE ) 

dbExecute( mycon, "ALTER TABLE test ADD PRIMARY KEY(id)" )
# Error : BLOB/TEXT column 'id' used in key specification without a key length [1170]

rs <- dbSendQuery( mycon, "SHOW COLUMNS FROM test" )
dbFetch(rs)

##  Field   Type Null Key Default Extra
##1   lib   text  YES        <NA>      
##2    id   text  YES        <NA>      
##3     x double  YES        <NA>    
```

title: Reenable DBItest and DBI remote
Bad Handshake when connecting to
description:
When connecting to a remote MySQL database using RMariaDB I get Bad Handshakes when using both Mac and Linux.

I'm calling 

    con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), 
        user = 'user', host = 'host', password = 'password',
        client.flag = RMariaDB::CLIENT_SSL)

The database requires SSL and without the client.flag I get an Access Denied error. Connecting to the database from the command line with the flag --ssl-mode=REQUIRED is totally fine. I'm really struggling to understand what the issue is.

description:
Hello,
When running the query "select * from table limit 10" all of the datetime fields returned have the value "1969-12-31 16:59:59", and is the case even when I filter the data (i.e. date_field >= '2017-08-10'). The data returned in all of the other fields is correct. I am running OSX and have seen this problem with R-version 3.4.1 and 3.3.3 (though I have only been able to replicate it on other OSX machines with R 3.3.3). This issue is not present when I use RMySQL.

Thanks,
Andrew

title: dbWriteTable writes Date values greater than 2038-01-19 as 1901-12-13
description:
I've noticed that the dbWriteTable command writes Date values greater than 2038-01-19 as 1901-12-13, but the issue does not arise if these are converted to character format first. I haven't tested extensively which dates are affected by this, but the example code below consistently replicates this issue on my system. 

```
dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), user=db.user, password=db.pass, dbname=db.name, host=db.host, ssl.ca=db.ssl.ca)
date.table <- data.frame(ID=c(1,2,3,4), parameter_value=as.Date(c('2017-01-01','2038-01-19','2039-01-20','2050-01-01')))
print(str(date.table))
#'data.frame':   4 obs. of  2 variables:
# $ ID             : num  1 2 3 4
# $ parameter_value: Date, format: "2017-01-01" "2038-01-19" ...

dbExecute(db.conn.rw, paste0("DELETE FROM test WHERE ID >= 1;"))
dbWriteTable(db.conn.rw, name="test", row.names = FALSE, value = date.table, append = TRUE)
print(dbGetQuery(db.conn.rw, paste0("SELECT * FROM test")))
#  ID parameter_value
#1  1      2017-01-01
#2  2      2038-01-19
#3  3      1901-12-13
#4  4      1901-12-13


#However, coercing the data to a character string results in the correct date being written to the database
date.table$parameter_value <- as.character(date.table$parameter_value) 
print(str(date.table))
#'data.frame':   4 obs. of  2 variables:
# $ ID             : num  1 2 3 4
# $ parameter_value: chr  "2017-01-01" "2038-01-19" "2039-01-20" "2050-01-01"

dbExecute(db.conn.rw, paste0("DELETE FROM test WHERE ID >= 1;"))
dbWriteTable(db.conn.rw, name="test", row.names = FALSE, value = date.table, append = TRUE)
print(dbGetQuery(db.conn.rw, paste0("SELECT * FROM test")))
#  ID parameter_value
#1  1      2017-01-01

title: dbWriteTable doesn't respect transactions
description:
Hello,

It appears transactions are used in the code for `RMariaDB::dbWriteTable`, which prevents users from rollingback insert queries. Perhaps there is a good reason for this, but it is not the case with `RMySQL`.

MRE:

```{R}
library(DBI)

conMySQL <- dbConnect(RMySQL::MySQL(),
                       host = host,
                       port = as.integer(port),
                       user = user,
                       password = password,
                       db = db)

conMariaDB <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                      host = host,
                      port = as.integer(port),
                      user = user,
                      password = password,
                      db = db)

# add fake data
dbWriteTable(conMySQL, "test1", data.frame(a = 1, b = 2), row.names = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(conMariaDB, "test2", data.frame(a = 1, b = 2), row.names = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

# insert data inside transaction
dbBegin(conMySQL)
dbBegin(conMariaDB)

# calling dbbegin twice should error but doesn't
dbBegin(conMySQL)
dbBegin(conMariaDB)

dbWriteTable(conMySQL, "test1", data.frame(a = 3, b = 4), row.names = FALSE, append = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(conMariaDB, "test2", data.frame(a = 3, b = 4), row.names = FALSE, append = TRUE)

dbGetQuery(conMySQL, "select * from test1")
dbGetQuery(conMariaDB, "select * from test2")

dbRollback(conMySQL)
dbRollback(conMariaDB)

dbGetQuery(conMySQL, "select * from test1")
# rollback unsuccesful
dbGetQuery(conMariaDB, "select * from test2")
```

Thank you for all your hard work with this wonderful package.

title: default options / default login in windows
description: **Issue by [jdthorpe](https://github.com/jdthorpe)** _Friday Nov 06, 2015 at 21:58 GMT_ _Originally opened as https://github.com/rstats-db/RMySQL/issues/102_ ---- First, the description of the `default.file` argumnet of the `dbConnect` in `RMySQL/R/connect.R` only applies to Unix-like OS's: ``` #' @param default.file string of the file name with MySQL client options. #' Defaults to \code{\$HOME/.my.cnf} ``` The locations of the options files in windows are described [here](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/option-files.html) and can also be found in these lines which appear about half way through the output returned by calling `% mysql --help`: ``` Default options are read from the following files in the given order: C:\Windows\my.ini C:\Windows\my.cnf C:\my.ini C:\my.cnf C:\Program Files\MySQL\my.ini C:\Program Files\MySQL\my.cnf ``` Second, in windows, the only way to have default connection settings with MySQL that aren't shared with all users of your computer is to use the [mysql_config_editor](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/mysql-config-editor.html) and create a set of (encrypted) login credentials. This works beautifully from the command line (via `c:\> mysql`), but does not seem to work with RMySQL: calling `dbConnect(RMySQL::MySQL(),groups="client")` raises an error. For example, on my machine, I get: ``` > con_sql <- dbConnect(MySQL()) Error in .local(drv, ...) : Failed to connect to database: Error: Access denied for user 'User Name'@'localhost' (using password: NO) > con_sql <- dbConnect(MySQL(),default.file=path.expand("~/.my.cnf")) > DBI::dbGetQuery(con_sql,"SELECT NOW()") NOW() 1 2015-11-07 00:11:14 ``` One can of course specify `dbConnect(... , default.file=path.expand("~/.my.cnf"))` to explicitly reference a saved `.my.cnf` file, but it would be great if RMySQL could use the same defaults as the `mysql` command line client. In the worst case, perhaps `default.file` could default to `getOption("default.file")`. Also, In case it's useful, here's my info: ``` > packageVersion("RMySQL") [1] ‘0.10.5’ > R.Version() $platform [1] "x86_64-w64-mingw32" $arch [1] "x86_64" $os [1] "mingw32" $system [1] "x86_64, mingw32" $status [1] "" $major [1] "3" $minor [1] "2.2" $year [1] "2015" $month [1] "08" $day [1] "14" $`svn rev` [1] "69053" $language [1] "R" $version.string [1] "R version 3.2.2 (2015-08-14)" $nickname [1] "Fire Safety" ```

title: Legacy mode available?
description: RMariaDB is meant to be a drop-in replacement for RMySQL, however it handles datatypes very differently. For example, BIGINTs are now imported as integer64 instead of numeric, and SQL Date columns are imported as Date instead of character. All of these are improvements, however as it is supposed to be "drop-in replacement", is there a "legacy" mode so that I can use this instead of RMySQL without rewriting all the scripts that depend on data read from it?

title: Cannot bind int64 (Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n) : Not yet supported )
description:
RMariaDB cannot bind int64. This is problematic as bigint is a very usefull and very common column type



```
install.packages("rlang"); #missing dependancy in RMariaDB
install.packages("RMariaDB");
install.packages("bit64"); #mariaDB uses this type, but nothing else works if this package is missing

library(DBI);
library(RMariaDB);
library(bit64);

drv <- RMariaDB::MariaDB()
db  <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="farm_sensors",host="127.0.0.1",user="xxx",password="xxx");
db
#<MariaDBConnection>
#  Host:    127.0.0.1
#  Server:  10.2.13-MariaDB
#  Client:  5.5.1


dbExecute(db,"create table test(x unsigned bigint)" );
dbExecute(db,"insert into test(x)values(18446744073709551615)");  #uint64 max
dbExecute(db,"insert into test(x)values(9223372036854775807)");   # int64 max



#--- bug1 : unsigned int interpreted as signed ---
dbGetQuery(db,"select * from test");
#                    x
#1                  -1
#2 9223372036854775807


#--- bug2 : cannot bind int 64 ---
d=list( as.integer64.character("42") )
dbGetQuery(db,"select * from test where x >=?",d  )
# Error in result_fetch(res@ptr, n) : Not yet supported



#--- NOTE : regular int works, but large values overflows ---
d=list( 42 )
dbGetQuery(db,"select * from test where x >=?",d  )
#                    x
#1                  -1
#2 9223372036854775807

```

title: handling of NaN is not DBI compliant
description:
setup: an integer column `col1` and a floating point col `col2` as

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), username = "test",
                      password = "***")

DBI::dbSendStatement(con, "CREATE TABLE `test` (col1 int, col2 double)")
```

writing `NaN` to the `int` column runs

```r
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "test", data.frame(col1 = c(1:3, NA, NaN),
                                          col2 = c(1:4, NA)),
                  append = TRUE)
```

but the result violates the DBI spec, as NaN should be translated to NA and not 0, as is the case:

```r
DBI::dbReadTable(con, "test")

#   col1 col2
# 1    1    1
# 2    2    2
# 3    3    3
# 4   NA    4
# 5    0    NA
```

writing `NaN` to a floating point col (both `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE`) fails entirely

```r
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "test", data.frame(col1 = NaN,
                                          col2 = NaN),
                  append = TRUE)

# Error during wrapup: Out of range value for column 'col2' at row 1 [1264]
```

title: Window functions and MariaDB
description:
Dear all,
I am not sure whether this is the correct place, but playing around with RMariaDB and trying to convert some statements into sql with `show_query()` I often get an error from dplyr stating that `... does not support window functions`. I am running MariaDB 10.2, the current stable, which *should* support window functions, at least that is what they state. The query I am sending of is
```
  BW <- somedata_db %>%
    group_by(key1) %>%
    filter(key2 == max(key2)) %>%
    summarise(val=max(key3))
```
Appending to this a `%>% show_query()` always ends in the "does not support" error.

Thanks a lot

Norbert

title: BLOB - RMariaDB vs RMySQL
description:
I have following case:

I am saving following data to blob field in DB, for example:

data <- as.raw(sample(1:32, 32))
data <- rawToChar(enc_key_raw)

 chr "\005 \036\020\a\017\n\024\b\002\035\030\003\037\t\v\026\f\001\031\034\032\025\023\027\033\006\004\r\021\022\016"

So when I am doing dbGetQuery() SELECT from db I was expecting to get same as return, but here is a case:

When switching to "RMySQL::MySQL()" connector I get exactly the same thing back:

 chr "\005 \036\020\a\017\n\024\b\002\035\030\003\037\t\v\026\f\001\031\034\032\025\023\027\033\006\004\r\021\022\016"

But when using RMariaDB::MariaDB() connector I get the following:

List of 1
 $ : raw [1:32] 05 20 1e 10 ..

 [1] 05 20 1e 10 07 0f 0a 14 08 02 1d 18 03 1f 09 0b 16 0c 01 19 1c 1a 15 13 17
[26] 1b 06 04 0d 11 12 0e

Can maybe someone please tell me why is this happening? Is this how it should behave or this is some-kind of bug?

The issue was I was using charToRaw on DB results and I did not got the same values as they should be initially, when using RMariaDB, since they are raw already...

description:

The following code does not work as expected:

```r

New tables named `db1.table1` and `db2.table1` are created in the default schema. Currently, I have to use `dbExecute(con, "use db1")` to switch databases but the drawback is that it permanently changes the state of my connection.

I'm wondering if there's a way to specify schema name in `dbWriteTable`?

title: DECIMAL handling
description:
It might make more sense to return DECIMAL columns as character vectors and not as as numeric.

Current mapping:
https://github.com/r-dbi/RMariaDB/blob/720b88933cb92b4995df4bad747e2bc6f8ab3278/src/MariaTypes.cpp#L19-L23

For some there might issues when converting exact numeric values to an approximate representation.

See also (from [here](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/c-api-prepared-statement-type-conversions.html))

> MySQL returns DECIMAL values as the string representation of the original server-side value, which is why the corresponding C type is char[]. For example, 12.345 is returned to the client as '12.345'. If you specify MYSQL_TYPE_NEWDECIMAL and bind a string buffer to the MYSQL_BIND structure, mysql_stmt_fetch() stores the value in the buffer as a string without conversion. If instead you specify a numeric variable and type code, mysql_stmt_fetch() converts the string-format DECIMAL value to numeric form.

title: Inconsistent behavior of time zone conversion

The database is set into UTC (GMT) +8 time zone (China). I have no problem in MySQL Workbench, while the date returned from RMariaDB is not what I expected sometimes.

Even though the session time zone is supposed to be set to UTC since version 0.11-1 (2016-03-24), the `from_unixtime` function of MySQL is still using +8 time zone, however `date` seems to be using UTC time zone.

At the mean time, RMySQL is returning things as I expected.

title: Issues with Date format if earlier than 1970-01-01
description:
Hi there,
R's been crashing when I try to dbWriteTable a data frame that contains Date fields with negative (pre-1970) values:

```
library(DBI)
conSQL <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(), etc etc)
datetest<-data.frame("today"=Sys.Date(),"yesterday"=Sys.Date()-1,"lastyear"=Sys.Date()-365)
dbWriteTable(conSQL,"DateTest",datetest, overwrite=TRUE)

### This runs OK ###
dbExecute(conSQL, "INSERT INTO `DateTest` VALUES ('2000-01-01','1970-01-01','1969-12-31');")

### This runs OK (Dates sent off as character type)
datetest<-data.frame("today"='2000-01-01',"yesterday"='1970-01-01',"lastyear"='1969-12-31')
dbWriteTable(conSQL,"DateTest",datetest, append=TRUE)

### This runs OK (Date type, but all after 1970) ###
datetest<-data.frame("today"=as.Date('2000-01-01'),"yesterday"=as.Date('1970-01-01'),"lastyear"=as.Date('2900-01-01'))
dbWriteTable(conSQL,"DateTest",datetest, append=TRUE)

### This crashes ###
datetest<-data.frame("today"=as.Date('2000-01-01'),"yesterday"=as.Date('1970-01-01'),"lastyear"=as.Date('1969-12-31'))
dbWriteTable(conSQL,"DateTest",datetest, append=TRUE)

dbDisconnect(conSQL)
```

The obvious workaround is to use character type, but it's inconvenient when the data is already in Date format in R. Both ends can encode dates in the past but something is wrong in translation when going from R to MariaDB (the reverse works fine). Because it crashes at exactly 1969-12-31, it's probably to do with R's Date format being a negative integer before 1970-01-01. Any help is appreciated!

title: "select 1" returns integer64
description:
I'm not sure if it is a desired behavior that a simple `select 1` query returns a data frame of an `integer64` column of `1`.

```r
> str(dbGetQuery(con, "select 1"))
'data.frame':	1 obs. of  1 variable:
 $ 1:integer64 1 
```

`odbc` returns `integer` with the same query. Personally, I think it is better to return integer64 only when it is necessary because the behavior of integer64 is in some aspects different from base R, e.g. integer64 times a double does not auto-convert to double.
